title: Bounded colimit apices and homotopy retracts are essentially small
statement: Use the universes, local smallness, essential smallness and $\beta$-small simplicial sets of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category], and coherent diagrams, mapping spaces and colimits of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $\mathcal E$ be a locally small quasicategory. Let $\mathcal G\subseteq\mathcal E$ be an essentially small full subcategory and $\beta$ an infinite regular cardinal in the smaller universe. The full subcategory of objects equivalent to apices of existing colimiting cocones $q:K\to\mathcal G\hookrightarrow\mathcal E$, as $K$ ranges over all $\beta$-small simplicial sets, is essentially small. Also the full subcategory of objects $x$ admitting maps $i:x\to g$ and $r:g\to x$ for some $g\in\mathcal G$ with $r i$ in the same connected component of $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(x,x)$ as $1_x$ is essentially small. No existence of the colimits or of splittings of arbitrary idempotents is assumed.

source.place: Proposition 5.4.1.7 and Proposition 5.4.1.2, printed pp. 419-423 (small object family plus local smallness); the bounded-diagram counting argument in Proposition 5.4.2.9, printed p. 426; the small retract-envelope argument in Lemma 5.4.2.4, printed pp. 424-425, and Section 5.1.4. The bounded-colimit and homotopy-retract variants are stated here as a general size-calculus consequence, not verbatim from one proposition. Read online, not archived under literature/. No Stacks tag supplies these coherent size assertions.

proof.text: Choose a small quasicategory $G_0$ and a functor equivalence $e:G_0\to\mathcal G$, with inverse $t$ and coherent natural equivalences of the composites with the identities. These data exist by the given essential smallness, as defined in [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category]. Write $j:\mathcal G\hookrightarrow\mathcal E$ for the full inclusion and $g_a=j e(a)$ for $a\in(G_0)_0$. The set of these indices is small. For each $g\in\mathcal G$, the comparison $e t(g)\simeq g$ gives an equivalence $g_{t(g)}\simeq j(g)$ in $\mathcal E$. If $\mathcal G$ is empty, $G_0$ is empty too; no nonemptiness is being assumed.

source.place: Proposition 5.4.1.7, printed p.423: use a small model of the essentially small subcategory. Agent expansion; this precise general variant is not asserted verbatim in HTT.

proof.text: There is a small set $T$ of simplicial sets containing an isomorphic representative of every $\beta$-small simplicial set. Here is a coding argument, including $\beta=\omega$. Every $n$-simplex is a degeneracy of a nondegenerate simplex of some dimension $m\le n$, by successively removing a degeneracy whenever one exists. For each fixed $n$ there are finitely many surjections $[n]\twoheadrightarrow[m]$. Thus if the total number of nondegenerate simplices is less than $\beta$, each degree has cardinal at most $\beta$. Choose a small set $B$ of cardinal $\beta$. Up to degreewise bijections, each degree is a subset of $B$, and each simplicial operator is a function between two such subsets. The countable family of degrees and operators can be coded by subsets and graphs in the fixed small set $\mathbb N\times\mathbb N\times B\times B$, together with the degree subsets. The codes satisfying the simplicial identities and the nondegenerate-simplex bound form a subset of a small power set. Take these codes as $T$. The empty simplicial set is among them. For every $K\in T$, the simplicial maps $K\to G_0$ form a small set: they are the families of functions $K_n\to(G_0)_n$ satisfying the simplicial equations. Consequently the pairs $(K,p)$ with $K\in T$ and $p:K\to G_0$ have a small index set $A$. This counts all coherence simplices, not only vertices and arrows.

source.place: Proposition 5.4.2.9, proof opening, printed p.426: expand the bounded-diagram counting argument. Agent expansion; this precise general variant is not asserted verbatim in HTT.

proof.text: Every diagram $q:K\to\mathcal G$ with $K$ $\beta$-small is represented by one of the pairs in $A$ up to isomorphism of its shape and coherent equivalence of its image in $\mathcal E$. Indeed choose a simplicial isomorphism $a:K_0\xrightarrow{\sim}K$ with $K_0\in T$ and put $p=t q a$. Whiskering the specified comparison $e t\simeq\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal G}$ by $q a$, then by $j$, gives a transformation $j e p\simeq j q a$. This is an equivalence in $\operatorname{Fun}(K_0,\mathcal E)$: its components are equivalences, so the vertex criterion in [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] applies. That same node ensures this functor simplicial set is a quasicategory for arbitrary simplicial $K_0$. Changing the shape by the actual isomorphism $a$ identifies the two functor categories and the two cocone categories degree by degree, including their constant-diagram maps and evaluations. Its inverse is restriction along $a^{-1}$, so it also identifies which cocones are initial.

source.place: Proposition 5.4.2.9, proof opening, printed p.426; Proposition 1.2.7.3 and the coherent cocone definitions supply the diagram comparison. Agent expansion; this precise general variant is not asserted verbatim in HTT.

proof.text: Coherently equivalent diagrams have the same possible colimit apices, and all colimit apices of a fixed diagram are equivalent. To check the first assertion, let $\alpha:p\xrightarrow{\sim}q$ be an equivalence in $D=\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal E)$ and let $\lambda:q\to\Delta_K x$ be colimiting. Compose to obtain $\lambda\alpha:p\to\Delta_Kx$ (choose an inner-triangle filler in $D$). For any $y\in\mathcal E$, the colimit test in the dual assertion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] gives an equivalence $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(x,y)\to\operatorname{Map}_D(q,\Delta_Ky)$. Precomposition with $\alpha$ is an equivalence from this last space to $\operatorname{Map}_D(p,\Delta_Ky)$: precomposition with an inverse edge is its homotopy inverse, by associativity and units in [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition], applied to $D$. The composite is the map induced by $\lambda\alpha$, up to the composition homotopy. The same colimit test proves this cocone colimiting. Applying the argument to an inverse of $\alpha$ proves the converse. For the second assertion, [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] says that the full subcategory of initial objects in the cocone category is a contractible Kan complex when nonempty. Hence any two colimiting cocones are equivalent there; the apex projection is a simplicial functor and preserves an equivalence together with its inverse-triangle witnesses. Their apices are therefore equivalent in $\mathcal E$. These arguments do not assume any further colimits exist.

source.place: Proposition 5.4.2.9, proof opening, printed p.426; expand invariance and uniqueness of existing colimits using their mapping-space universal property. Agent expansion; this precise general variant is not asserted verbatim in HTT.

proof.text: Let $A'\subseteq A$ consist of exactly the pairs $(K,p)$ for which $j e p$ admits a colimit in $\mathcal E$. This is a small set. For each such pair choose one existing colimiting cocone and call its apex $L_{K,p}$. This is a small-indexed family of objects in the larger universe; no choice is made for a diagram without a colimit. Steps 3 and 4 show that every apex in the first clause is equivalent to one of these $L_{K,p}$, and each chosen apex belongs to that clause. Thus its full replete subcategory is exactly the full subcategory on objects equivalent to this small-indexed family. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-small-full-subcategory] to the locally small $\mathcal E$ and that family. This proves the bounded-colimit clause. If $A'$ is empty the cited node explicitly allows the empty family. When $\mathcal G$ is empty, the empty diagram remains in $A$; it contributes precisely when $\mathcal E$ has an initial object.

source.place: Proposition 5.4.1.7, printed p.423, and the bounded-apex argument in Proposition 5.4.2.9, printed p.426. Agent expansion; this precise general variant is not asserted verbatim in HTT.

proof.text: For the retract clause, [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition] supplies the ordinary category $h\mathcal E$ with $\operatorname{Hom}_{h\mathcal E}(x,y)=\pi_0\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(x,y)$, and says that invertible morphism classes are precisely equivalence edges. Its hom sets are small up to bijection: local smallness provides a small space equivalent to each mapping space, hence a small set of its components. The condition on $i,r$ in the statement is exactly $[r][i]=1_x$ in this category. If $g\in\mathcal G$ and $g\simeq g_a$ is one of the equivalences of step 1, represented in $h\mathcal E$ by mutually inverse arrows $s:g\to g_a$ and $u:g_a\to g$, replace $[i]$ by $s[i]$ and $[r]$ by $[r]u$. Their composite is $[r]us[i]=1_x$. Thus every homotopy retract in question is a splitting of an idempotent on one of the small family $g_a$, in $h\mathcal E$.

source.place: Lemma 5.4.2.4, printed pp.424-425, small retract-envelope assertion; the ordinary homotopy-category reduction is written out rather than assuming coherent idempotent completeness. Agent expansion; this precise general variant is not asserted verbatim in HTT.

proof.text: For each $a$, choose a small set in bijection with $\operatorname{End}_{h\mathcal E}(g_a)$. The pairs $(a,e)$ with $e^2=e$ therefore form a small set $I$. Restrict to the subset $I'\subseteq I$ for which there actually exist an object $x_e$ and arrows $i_e:x_e\to g_a$, $r_e:g_a\to x_e$ in $h\mathcal E$ with $r_e i_e=1_{x_e}$ and $i_e r_e=e$, and choose one such triple for each member of $I'$. A retract $x\xrightarrow{i}g_a\xrightarrow{r}x$ with $ri=1_x$ yields $e=ir$ and $e^2=i(ri)r=ir$, so $(a,e)\in I'$. Compare it with the chosen splitting: set $v=r_e i:x\to x_e$ and $w=r i_e:x_e\to x$. Then $wv=r(i_e r_e)i=r e i=r(ir)i=1_x$, and $vw=r_e(ir)i_e=r_e e i_e=r_e(i_e r_e)i_e=1_{x_e}$. These are ordinary categorical calculations in the category supplied in step 6. Thus $x$ and $x_e$ are isomorphic in $h\mathcal E$, and hence equivalent in $\mathcal E$ by [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition]. Only idempotents with an existing splitting were selected; no claim that an arbitrary homotopy idempotent splits has entered.

source.place: Section 5.1.4 and Lemma 5.4.2.4, printed pp.424-425; explicit uniqueness-of-a-splitting calculation for the weaker homotopy-retract relation used here. Agent expansion; this precise general variant is not asserted verbatim in HTT.

proof.text: Every chosen $x_e$ is a homotopy retract of its $g_a\in\mathcal G$: the arrows $i_e,r_e$ in $h\mathcal E$ have edge representatives by [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition], and their equation means exactly the component equality required by the statement. The homotopy-retract property is invariant under equivalence of $x$: if $b:x'\xrightarrow{\sim}x_e$ in $h\mathcal E$, use $i_e b:x'\to g_a$ and $b^{-1}r_e:g_a\to x'$; their composite is $b^{-1}(r_e i_e)b=1_{x'}$. Step 7 shows conversely that every object in the retract clause is equivalent to a chosen $x_e$. Its full subcategory is therefore exactly the full subcategory on the replete closure of the small family $(x_e)_{e\in I'}$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-small-full-subcategory] in the locally small $\mathcal E$. The empty-family case includes $\mathcal G=\varnothing$. This proves the second clause without requiring an idempotent completion of $\mathcal E$.

source.place: Proposition 5.4.1.7, printed p.423; complete the small-retract-envelope argument underlying Lemma 5.4.2.4. Agent expansion; this precise general variant is not asserted verbatim in HTT.
